chunks: And it is narrated from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man comes upon his brother while he is in tawaf.
So he said: He may go out with him regarding his need, then return and continue from his tawaf.

key_terms.أَخَاهُ: his fellow brother, meaning another Muslim or companion
key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: circumambulation around the Kaʿbah during hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.حَاجَتِهِ: his need or matter requiring assistance
key_terms.يَبْنِي: he continues on what he had already completed

ai.seo_question: Can someone interrupt tawaf to help another person and then continue from where he stopped?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one whose tawaf is interrupted in order to attend to the need of another Muslim. It indicates that he may leave, help his brother, then return and resume his tawaf from where he stopped, showing both flexibility in ritual practice and regard for the needs of others.
